Scafell Pike.credit: Thorneh at English Wikipedia, Public domain
Scafell Pike.about: England's highest mountain: a bouldery dome topped by a huge summit cairn, a trig point and the war memorial plaque given with the summit to the National Trust.

routes.name: Wasdale Head via Brown Tongue
routes.text: The shortest way. Up Lingmell Gill and the steep pitched path of Brown Tongue into Hollow Stones, then left up the bouldery slope to the top.

routes.name: Seathwaite via the Corridor Route
routes.text: From Borrowdale by Stockley Bridge to Sty Head, then the Corridor Route across the flank of Great End and Lingmell to the summit plateau.

routes.name: Great Langdale via Esk Hause
routes.text: Up Mickleden and Rossett Gill to Angle Tarn and Esk Hause, then the rough boulder ridge over Ill Crag and Broad Crag.

Scafell.about: Scafell Pike's rockier, quieter neighbour across the gap of Mickledore. Broad Stand, the direct way between them, is a serious rock climb, not a walk.

routes.name: Wasdale Head via Green How
routes.text: A relentless grassy slope from Brackenclose straight up the west side; the easiest way up, if steep.

routes.name: From Scafell Pike via Foxes Tarn
routes.text: Drop from Mickledore on the Eskdale side, then climb the gully past tiny Foxes Tarn. The usual way to add Scafell to the Pike.

routes.name: Eskdale via Slight Side
routes.text: From Boot across the moor past Eel Tarn to Slight Side, then up the long south ridge. Long and quiet.

Helvellyn.about: The Lakes' most popular big fell: a broad summit plateau above the Red Tarn corrie, held between the arms of Striding Edge and Swirral Edge.

routes.name: Glenridding via Striding Edge
routes.text: The classic scramble. Up to the Hole-in-the-Wall, along the exposed rocky crest of Striding Edge, then a steep loose wall to the plateau.

routes.name: Glenridding via Swirral Edge
routes.text: Past Red Tarn and up the shorter, easier ridge beside Catstye Cam; the usual way down after Striding Edge.

routes.name: Thirlmere from Swirls
routes.text: The quickest way: a steep pitched path over Browncove Crags from the Swirls car park on the A591.

routes.name: Bridleway along the ridge
routes.text: The main ridge path from Grisedale Tarn over Dollywaggon and Nethermost Pike to the summit, and north towards Whiteside, is a public bridleway: a hard, rocky but legal ride.

Skiddaw.about: A great slaty whaleback above Keswick, with a long, stony summit ridge and a trig point; one of the few big Lakeland summits on a bridleway.

routes.name: Keswick via Jenkin Hill
routes.text: From the car park above Latrigg, the broad 'tourist' path climbs Jenkin Hill and skirts Little Man. Long and steady, and a bridleway all the way to the summit.

routes.name: Millbeck via Carl Side
routes.text: Steep and direct from Millbeck up Carl Side, then loose scree to the summit ridge.

routes.name: Back o' Skiddaw via Bakestall
routes.text: From the road end near Peter House Farm, the track past Whitewater Dash waterfall, then the steep Bakestall ridge from the north.

Great End.about: The dark, gully-scored northern end of the Scafell massif, looming over Sprinkling Tarn and Borrowdale. Its gullies are classic winter climbs.

routes.name: Seathwaite via Grains Gill
routes.text: Up Grains Gill and Ruddy Gill to Esk Hause, then turn north-west up the broad slope to the summit cairns.

routes.name: Great Langdale via Rossett Gill
routes.text: Over Rossett Pass and past Angle Tarn to Esk Hause, then up the stony slope.

routes.name: With Scafell Pike
routes.text: Often added on the way to or from the Pike: about 1.5 km of boulders over Ill Crag and Broad Crag.

Bowfell.credit: GkgAlf at English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 3.0
Bowfell.about: A shapely rock peak at the head of Great Langdale. The Great Slab and the Climbers' Traverse on its north-east face are among the Lakes' best walking terrain.

routes.name: Great Langdale via The Band
routes.text: From the Old Dungeon Ghyll, up the long ridge of The Band to Three Tarns, then north over the boulder-strewn final cone.

routes.name: The Climbers' Traverse
routes.text: From the top of The Band, a narrow path under Flat Crags to the Great Slab and a steep, rocky finish. More interesting, a little more exposed.

routes.name: Eskdale via Lingcove Beck
routes.text: A long, quiet approach from Brotherilkeld up Lingcove Beck to Three Tarns.

Great Gable.credit: Phillip Capper from Wellington, New Zealand, CC BY 2.0
Great Gable.about: The rock pyramid between Wasdale and Borrowdale. A bronze war memorial on the summit crag draws a crowd every Remembrance Sunday.

routes.name: Honister via Green Gable
routes.text: From the slate mine, up the old tramway to the Drum House, then over Brandreth and Green Gable to Windy Gap and a steep rocky finish. Starts high.

routes.name: Wasdale Head via Sty Head
routes.text: Up the valley to Sty Head, then the steep, rocky south-east ridge.

routes.name: Seathwaite via Sty Head
routes.text: Stockley Bridge and Styhead Gill to Sty Head, then the same rough ridge.

Pillar.about: The highest fell between Wasdale and Ennerdale, named after Pillar Rock, the great crag on its northern face, first climbed in 1826.

routes.name: Wasdale Head via Black Sail Pass
routes.text: Up Mosedale to Black Sail Pass, then west along the ridge over Looking Stead.

routes.name: The High Level Route
routes.text: From Looking Stead, a narrow, exposed path traverses under the north face to Robinson's Cairn and Pillar Rock, then climbs steeply to the top.

routes.name: Ennerdale
routes.text: From Bowness Knott, the long Ennerdale forest road (good on a bike) to the head of the valley, then up from Black Sail Hut. A big day.

Nethermost Pike.about: A flat-topped summit on the Helvellyn ridge just south of the main top, with a steep craggy face above Grisedale. Many people pass by without noticing it.

routes.name: Along the ridge from Helvellyn
routes.text: Under a kilometre south along the broad ridge; the main path skirts the top, so step west to find the cairn.

routes.name: Wythburn
routes.text: From Wythburn church on Thirlmere, up the pitched path to the ridge, then north.

routes.name: Grisedale via the east ridge
routes.text: From Patterdale along Grisedale, then up the steep, rough and quiet east ridge.

routes.name: Bridleway along the ridge
routes.text: The ridge path from Grisedale Tarn to Helvellyn, beside the summit, is a public bridleway.

Catstye Cam.about: A perfect little cone at the end of Swirral Edge, and the best perch above Red Tarn.

routes.name: Glenridding via Red Tarn Beck
routes.text: Past the old Greenside lead mine and up Red Tarn Beck, then the steep path onto the north-east ridge.

routes.name: From Swirral Edge
routes.text: A short there-and-back from the foot of Swirral Edge on the way up or down Helvellyn.
